artifacts.summary: Confirms the validate-state.sh CWD-relative default defect, verifies common_repo_root()'s fixed-hop-count is unsuitable (differs by layout), recommends git-toplevel-of-SCRIPT_DIR upward discovery (reusing test-validate-state.sh's own existing REPO_ROOT idiom) as the fix, and completes the Part (b) sibling survey with a per-site verdict.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/lib/common.sh's common_repo_root(script_dir, levels) takes a caller-supplied fixed hop count and gives a WRONG (layout-dependent) answer for any scripts/ caller whose deployed-tree and source-store copies sit at different depths below the repo root (e.g. .claude/scripts/ at depth 2 vs. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ at depth 4). Prefer git-toplevel-of-SCRIPT_DIR upward discovery (git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel, fixed-hop fallback only if that fails) for any script required to run unmodified from both locations -- this is already the technique scripts/tests/test-validate-state.sh uses for its own REPO_ROOT.

Before treating a bare 'specs/state.json'-style relative reference in a scripts/*.sh caller as a cross-repo defect, check whether the file already `cd`s to a caller-supplied, pre-resolved repo-root variable (e.g. orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's `cd "$SKILL_REPO_ROOT"` near its top) before reaching that reference -- CWD-relative-after-pinning is a different, non-defective case from an unguarded ambient-CWD dependency.
